### Round 532 — a code block's Copy control confirms for one second

**The gap.** The reference's code block flips its copy button from `Copy code` to `Copied` for one
second after a successful clipboard write (`ui-primitives/src/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx:156-170`). Native
wrote the clipboard and said "Code copy requested." in the app's status line — never on the control the
press belongs to.

**The change.** `App.code_copied` holds `(reply key, document block index)` for one second; the copy
action now batches the clipboard write with a one-second timer that clears exactly that pair, and
`copied_code(key)` hands the index to the reply's view. `code_copy_label(copied, index)` is the label
rule, so a press on one block never confirms another block of the same reply, and a stale timer cannot
clear a newer confirmation.

block 0, but the copy action and the label both index **document blocks** (`PreparedReply::code` reads
`blocks.get(index)`), and the first fenced block follows a paragraph. Seeding block 1 — the block the
press would carry — put `Copied` on the first banner and left the second at `Copy code`.

fix): the `rust` block's banner reading `Copied`, the `bash` block beneath it still `Copy code`.

### Round 533 — a code card wraps by default, and one block can turn that off

**The gap.** The reference's reply code blocks render the **card** variant: `MarkdownText` passes
`copyLabel`/`copiedLabel`/`toolbarLabels` to `CodeBlock`, so the banner carries a language label, a
wrap toggle and a copy control, and the card's own default is `wrapped = true` — `pre-wrap` with a
`No wrap` action to return to preserved columns
(`ui-primitives/src/markdown/render.tsx:394-410`, `CodeBlock.tsx:156-166`,
`CodeCard.module.css:113-134`). Native always drew `Wrapping::None` inside a horizontal scroll: every
long line was permanently in the *unwrapped* state, with no way back and no control that said so.

**The change.** Wrapping is per block and defaults to on. `CodeWrap` holds the document block indices a
reader unwrapped; it lives on `Prepared` (so the height cache and the render read one source) and
`set_code_wrap` clears the measured heights when it changes, because a wrapped block is taller.
`block_height`, `document_height`, `document_first_offset` and `document_view` take it, so the reserve
and the paint agree. A wrapped block measures at `width - 2 * CODE_PAD` with word wrapping and no
scrollable; an unwrapped one keeps one line's height and scrolls sideways. The banner gains the
reference's toggle — `No wrap` while wrapped, `Wrap` while not — beside the copy control.

**Frame.** `shots/327-code-wrapped.png` (1040x560, new `code-wrapped` preset): one long `rust` line
wrapped across two lines inside the card, whose height grew to hold both, with `No wrap` and
`Copy code` on the banner.

the press unwraps exactly that block (not its neighbour, not another reply), the label flips to `Wrap`,
and a second press restores wrapping.

### Round 539 — a terminal's title can be renamed

**The gap.** The coverage table and `docs/NATIVE-TERMINAL.md` both recorded rename as unbuilt: the Host
serves `terminal/rename` (1–120 characters, trimmed, refused when empty or unchanged), and the panel
offered no way to reach it.

**The change, end to end.** The transport gains `Endpoint::TerminalRename` and
`terminal_rename(address, id, title)`, gated by `terminal::validate_title` (the Host's own rule, plus a
control-character refusal so a newline can never split the panel's row); the worker gains
`Command::TerminalRename` on the shared terminal flight and `Event::TerminalRenamed`; the terminal model
gains a rename review (opened on the Host's current title, editable, refused locally when the title is
empty, over 120 characters, control-bearing or unchanged), `RenameReceipt`/`RenameSubmission`, and
`finish_rename`, which installs the title only from an ACK for the reviewed terminal; and the panel
draws `Rename…` per listed terminal with a review row — a labelled title field, Back and Confirm rename.

### Round 540 — the terminal can be resized

**The gap.** `docs/NATIVE-TERMINAL.md` recorded in-panel resize as unbuilt, and the panel always asked
for an `80×24` PTY. The Host serves `terminal/resize` (bounded by the limits it advertises), and the
transport already carried `terminal_resize` with `validate_dimensions`; nothing above the transport
reached it.

**The change.** The model gains a resize review (`ReviewResize`, `BackResize`, `EditResize`,
`ConfirmResize`) opened on the size the Host reports for the selected terminal, editable within the
limits the Host advertised, refused locally for zero, out-of-bounds or unchanged dimensions, with
`ResizeReceipt`/`ResizeSubmission` fenced to the panel's writable attachment and `finish_resize`
adopting the size only from the Host's ACK. The worker gains `Command::TerminalResize` on the shared
terminal flight and `Event::TerminalResized`; the panel draws `Resize…` per row with a review row of two
labelled fields, Back and Confirm resize. `busy()`, dismiss, the disconnect fence and the smoke
example's command-kind match learned the new flight.

**Deliberate difference, recorded.** The reference's terminal **fits to its pane automatically** through
the emulator it mounts; native has no screen to fit, so resize is an explicit reviewed control. The
reference's continuous fit therefore remains unbuilt; the ability to change the PTY size does not.

**Frame.** `shots/334-terminal-resize.png` (1200x900, new `terminal-resize` preset): the row reading
`Resize… · Rename… · Close…`, the review line "Resize PUBLIC-terminal-1: columns 1–80, rows 1–24. The
Host refuses a size it never advertised.", fields holding `72` and `18`, `Back` / `Confirm resize`, and
the notice "Review the dimensions, then Confirm resize." The first seeds used out-of-bounds sizes
(120x40, then 100x20) and were corrected before the frame was kept.

**Tests.** `a_resize_is_reviewed_bounded_and_installed_only_from_the_ack` (an attached panel reviews the
reported size, edits it, emits exactly one Host update, and adopts the size only from the ACK) and
`a_resize_of_zero_an_unchanged_size_or_beyond_the_limits_is_refused` (0 columns, 0 rows, the unchanged
size, over-limit columns and over-limit rows each refused locally).

### Round 541 — a schedule changed elsewhere reloads an open catalog

**The gap.** The coverage table carried this as a **user-only verification**: "a `schedule/changed` live
refresh is unverified — the Host's event contract for it has never been observed in a run, so native
reads the catalog only on open, Refresh, and after its own writes." The reference's own client
re-reads on that notification (`ui-schedule/src/client/catalog-source.ts:173`, `index.ts:99-100`), and
the Host emits it after every durable schedule write with the emitter's failure contained
(`packages/schedule/schedule/src/index.ts:376-386`).

**What the code already had.** Native's transport opens the `$events` stream and parses forwarded
`Emit` frames, and the UI already routes `Emit` events by name (`api-session/*`,
`goal/activation-changed`). Nothing was missing except the arm for this notification, so the earlier
"unverified" label understated what could be built safely: the wire path and the emitter both exist.

**The change.** `root()`'s `Emit` match gains `"schedule/changed"`: when the Schedules page or the
reminders popover is open it marks the catalog loading and issues the same `ScheduleCatalog` read the
Refresh control uses. A closed catalog issues nothing, so the notification costs no request when no one
is looking.

**Tests.** `a_schedule_change_from_the_host_reloads_an_open_catalog` — no read with both surfaces closed;
exactly one read with the page open, and `schedules_loading` set; exactly one with only the reminders
popover open.

**Still user-only, stated precisely.** The arm is test-covered and the Host's emission is
source-confirmed, but no live run has yet shown the notification arriving on a real session: that needs
the user's running Host and a schedule changed from another client. Until then the coverage table says
"arm built and unit-tested; live arrival unobserved".

**No frame:** this round changes behaviour, not pixels.

**The gap, as recorded.** Round 278 carried this as a standing "Not claimed": live Host arrival of the
`tokenUsage`/`inbox` projections was unverified because the fixture seeded them. Round 522's
`turnOutline` qualifier had in fact already published both keys in its snapshot (19 client-visible
units) — nobody had connected that evidence to this claim, which is its own failure class: a verified
fact recorded as unverified hides the work that remains.

**What this round adds.** `scripts/qualify-client-projections.mjs` boots the pinned alpha runtime
through the app's own fork supervisor (isolated home, base+web profile), creates one blank session and
reads `ctx.sessionProjections.snapshot(session)` — the same registry read every follow frame and
control baseline is built from (`packages/api/session-controller/src/control.ts:62-82`) — then checks
the twelve keys native's chat consumes against a named table: `turnOutline` (rail marks and previews),
`tokenUsage` (usage pill and statistics dialog), `inbox` (queued-message classification),
`contextPressure`, `contextBreakdown`, `modelSelection`, `plan`, `todos`, `subagent`, `userQuestions`,
`title`, `sessionStats`. `scripts/qualify-client-projections.py` runs it through the existing
pidfd-owned runner and validates the report.

**Result — passed.** `app/evidence/client-projections-20261019-195516/result.json`: status `passed`,
exit 0, source unchanged, cleanup complete. Facts: `registryPresent`, `allNamedKeysPublished`,
`blankSessionShapes` all true, `missing` empty, **19** client-visible units published, and the blank
session's shapes are real (`turnOutline` an empty list, `tokenUsage` an object or null rather than
absent).

**Scope, stated exactly.** This is a Host-side composition and snapshot check, not a native transport or
GUI run: it proves the keys are published for a session, not that the mux delivered them to Rust in a
live session (the transport's projection retention is unit-tested). No model, catalog or credential path
is started — `modelPromptsRequested` and `catalogRequested` are false. No frame: nothing visual changed.

### Round 544 — the wrapped code card's height rule, measured and pinned

**The gap.** Round 533 made code cards wrap by default and put the wrap state on the reply so
`block_height` and the paint read one value — but no test compared the two heights. That is the exact
shape of the bug round 531's frame caught (a reservation that disagrees with the paint clips the last
line), so the rule needed a measurement test rather than a state test.

**The test.** `a_wrapped_code_card_reserves_the_lines_it_will_draw` parses a fenced block holding one
200-character line and asserts what the two states reserve at a 400px lane: the wrapped card is
strictly taller, the unwrapped card is exactly `design::CODE_CHROME + one code line`, and a block that
fits on one wrapped line reserves the same height either way. The unwrapped state is built through the
same `CodeWrap::for_reply` the app uses, so the test exercises the production seam rather than a
hand-built struct.

**The doc.** `docs/NATIVE-CHAT-GEOMETRY.md` gains the rule beside its other reservation contracts: the
wrapped card measures at `width - 2 * CODE_PAD` with word wrapping, the unwrapped one keeps one line
and scrolls, and both read `Prepared::set_code_wrap`. The document previously described only the
tool-body diff card, so a reader of the geometry contract could not tell there were two code heights.

**No frame:** the frame that shows a wrapped card already exists (`shots/327-code-wrapped.png`, round
533); this round proves the number behind it.

### Round 545 — a repo-wide citation sweep

**Why.** Round 543's four-document sweep found a dead helper and a vanished test, which is a cheap way
to find real drift: the docs cite test names, functions and files constantly, and a rename or deletion
leaves the citation pointing at nothing. This round ran the same check over **every** doc.

**Method.** For each `*.md` under `docs/`, extract every backticked identifier matching
`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` with at least two underscores and 18+ characters, then look it up textually across
`app/src`, `app/examples`, `transport/src`, `transport/tests`, `core/src` and `scripts`. Anything with no
match is a candidate; each candidate was then read in context, because a name can be legitimately
historical.

**Result — five candidates, one real drift.**

| candidate | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `heading_margins_step_up_like_the_reference` | already annotated as superseded in round 543 |
| `a_group_seat_sits_inside_its_first_row_and_reserves_only_its_own_line` | already records its own rename in round 512 |
| `unsupported_document_preserves_complete_source_and_nonce_exhaustion_disables_actions` | **real drift**: renamed in round 538; the round-528 note now carries a superseded pointer that names the current test |
| `chat_geometry_probe` | false positive: an example *target*, which exists on disk but whose name is not inside the sources the sweep read |
| `too_many_arguments` | false positive: a rustc lint name |

Everything else in sixty-odd documents matched the tree. The round-528 note was also annotated where it
says titled images and links "stay refused" — they parse since round 529 — so a linear reader is not
left believing a construct is refused when it is not.

**No code, no frame:** the sweep found documentation drift only, and the one code-adjacent claim it
touched (a test name) was corrected in the docs rather than by renaming the test back.
